proposed.text: Under PD 1096 Rule XII, Sec. 1207, what is the minimum clear width of corridors serving all occupancies covered by that section?

options.text: 0.90 m — the minimum width for private residential corridors and short stair flights
1.10 m — the Code-prescribed minimum corridor width for all occupancies under Sec. 1207
1.20 m — the standard minimum for pedestrian walkways under construction protection
1.50 m — required only for institutional occupancies with non-ambulatory patients

proposed.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: Sec. 1207 prescribes a single minimum corridor width of 1.10 m for all occupancies within its scope. There are no sub-category variations — 1.10 m applies universally. The 0.90 m figure is the minimum door clear width, not the corridor width.
proposed.explanation: The single universal minimum (1.10 m) is frequently confused with stair widths or door widths. Sec. 1207 sets no occupancy-specific corridor variations — any answer listing different widths for different occupancies is incorrect.
